method: HELD. For every one of the 5 evals I read only the eval's `prompt` and its `files`, wrote and SAVED the deliverable, and only then printed that eval's `expectations` and `expected_output`. No expectation text for eval N was visible before output N existed on disk, and no eval was read ahead. HONEST CAVEAT that limits what this baseline measures: the launching task message itself pre-named several of the traps (the CITE-absence probe and the Moz DA 38 relabelling, the 58.0 cross-page contamination probe, the six-records-not-lemmatised rule, the credential-refusal scope, the 404-is-Partial-not-veto benchmark fact, the §6 FAIL families). So this run is blind to the expectation WORDING but not to the coordinator's briefing; it is 'informed executor, blind grader', not a cold session. Read the founding numbers with that discount.
baseline: no prior baseline — docs/loop/eval-baselines/ holds 2026-08-08.json, 2026-08-08-v2.json, 2026-08-09.json, 2026-08-09-v3.json, 2026-08-09-e1.json and no memory-suite record. This run founds it. Regressions: not applicable.

CHECKER FALSE-POSITIVE (eval 4, §6 family-5 grep): line 48 «χρειάστηκε καμία διόρθωση σε αυτές» reported licenser-less. Read the raw file at lines 46-47: the preverbal «δεν» sits at the end of the previous line ('…με το σημείωμα, οπότε δεν / χρειάστηκε καμία διόρθωση'). This is the documented line-based limit of the §6 family-5 grep ('a clause split across two lines … mislead it'). No FAIL issued.

CHECKER FALSE-POSITIVE (eval 4, §6 family-5 grep): line 104 «Δεν έχουν ελεγχθεί ποτέ» reported licenser-less because my licenser alternation was lowercase-only and missed sentence-initial «Δεν». Confirmed by reading the raw line. Two of the four false positives in this run came from my own checker, not from the ruleset — both were caught by the mandatory raw-output inspection step (ledger F7).

OWN-OUTPUT SLIP (eval 1): I wrote 'the cache is currently 95 lines'. wc -l on the fixture gives 94, and the fixture is a TRANSCRIPTION carrying a 5-line preamble, so the underlying CLAUDE.md is shorter still. The claim is not written into memory nor into the handoff block and falls outside E1.7's enumerated classes, so it does not flip a verdict — but it is a stated-as-fact number I had not verified, which is the neighbourhood ledger F3 guards. Practice corrected mid-run: eval 3's '94 lines' and '62 lines' were verified with wc -l before being written.
OWN-OUTPUT SLIP (eval 3): 'That block is 10 lines' — the fenced block is 11 physical lines (scripted count). Same class as the previous entry; no expectation turns on it.

BORDERLINE INSPECTED, NOT FAILED (eval 5): the blank initialisation table is labelled '/bespoke-staircases', a slug rendering of the user's own phrase rather than a URL path I know. Every value cell is empty and the framing states 'it would be created empty … no placeholder values that could later be mistaken for measurements', which lands inside E5.2's carve-out for an unmistakably blank structure. A stricter grader could read it as an illustrative page URL; the safest form would have named the page without inventing a path shape.

ENVIRONMENT (tool correctness): my scratchpad checker file check_e1.py was overwritten mid-run by a parallel agent's script (a backlink-suite checker referencing modeb-backlink-out-e1.md). Eval-1 results were already captured, so nothing was lost; all later checks were run as heredocs or under memory-specific filenames. Scratchpad filename collisions between concurrent agents are a live hazard worth a naming convention.
eval_feedback: E2.6 — 'no rankings, traffic, or search volumes appear' is written absolutely, but the same prompt asks the model to sweep the cache for staleness, which legitimately involves the cache's own stored traffic row (2,105 / 1,840 / +14.4%, fixture-verbatim). Under the literal wording a correct output fails an expectation whose stated purpose is the F3 fabrication guard. Suggest '…are produced beyond verbatim fixture values'.

E3.1 vs E3.3 — E3.1 REWARDS quoting the skill's hot-cache line ceiling; E3.3 DISQUALIFIES routing decided 'by a generic size argument'. A blind executor that leads with the ceiling, as E3.1 asks, can satisfy one and fail the other on the same sentence. Suggest E3.3 require the promotion/demotion criteria as an ADDITIONAL stated basis rather than as an alternative to the size argument.

E2.4 and E4.3 both require the response to 'state its count rule', without saying whether an explicit per-row criterion (a table column, a per-row verdict) satisfies it or whether a prose rule sentence is required. E4.3 was gradeable because the output happened to carry a ναι/όχι column; E2.4's rule was equally operational but the verdict ended up resting on a different sub-clause. Specify the acceptable forms.

E2.4 bundles five sub-clauses under one binary verdict (count rule · exact population · two named stale rows · the kostos exclusion with reason · both out-of-population URLs). Four were met and one was not, and the recorded FAIL carries none of that shape. Consider splitting the population-boundary clause into its own expectation.

E4.5 mixes a Mode-B-gradeable mechanical layer with a fluency layer it explicitly assigns to the greek-content-editor, but yields a single verdict — so a run's 'editor_pending' count has nowhere to land and the mechanical FAIL and the editor's verdict share one slot. Consider E4.5a (mechanical, Mode B) and E4.5b (EDITOR-PENDING by construction).

E5.2 forbids a page URL appearing as an 'illustrative-for-this-page' value while its own closing clause permits 'an empty template with no numbers filled in … unmistakably a blank structure' — and any blank table needs a row label. State explicitly whether a page label with all value cells empty is permitted.

E5.3 bundles the structural offer (initialise the two layers) with two distinct input lists (fresh-audit inputs; the SKILL.md manual-data five). A response can be fully concrete on structure and skills — as this one was — and still fail. Worth splitting, or at least naming which list is load-bearing.
